learning_outcomes.text: identify and distinguish various layered reference models
identify and describe the main functionalities of each layer of the OSI and TCP/IP reference models
be able to solve problems and study cases for each of the first three layers of the OSI reference model
be able to conduct experiments, record and analyze their results and assess the behavior and performance of different technologies
be able to assess the performance of different technologies using analytic and simulation tools.

syllabus_topics: Classification of networks and their technologies
Services, protocols and reference models (OSI and TCP/IP)
Error and flow control protocols and their performance
Interconnection of local area networks (VLANs and STPs)
Routing and forwarding. Architecture of a router.
Addressing in IPv4 and IPv6 protocols. NAT.
Network interconnection. RIP, OSPF, and BGP routing protocols.
Key Internet protocols: ICMP, ARP and DHCP.
assessment_rules: There are two modes of assessment: throughout the semester or by exam. For assessment throughout the semester, a minimum mark of 8.0 (out of 20) is required for the written test. For exam evaluation, both the written and practical parts must be done in the same exam season, and the written part requires a minimum mark of 8 (out of 20).
